blocks.explanation:
This series is not a G.P. (\(\frac{0.22}{0.2} = 1.1\) but \(\frac{0.222}{0.22} \approx 1.009\)).
Trick: take out 2, multiply and divide by 9, so each term becomes \(1\) minus a power of \(\frac{1}{10}\).
Plan: split into "\(n\) ones" minus a G.P., and sum that G.P.
steps:
Given: \(0.2 + 0.22 + 0.222 + \cdots\) to \(n\) terms.
To find: \(S_n\).
Method: Rewrite each term so a G.P. appears, then use \(S_n = \frac{a_1(1 - r^{n})}{1 - r}\).

Take out the common factor 2
\[S_n = 2(0.1 + 0.11 + 0.111 + \cdots)\]
Why: \(0.2 = 2 \times 0.1\), \(0.22 = 2 \times 0.11\), and so on.

Multiply and divide by 9
\[S_n = \dfrac{2}{9}(0.9 + 0.99 + 0.999 + \cdots)\]
Why: \(\frac{9}{9} = 1\) does not change the value, and \(9 \times 0.1 = 0.9\), \(9 \times 0.11 = 0.99\), \(9 \times 0.111 = 0.999\).

Write each term as 1 minus a small number
\[S_n = \dfrac{2}{9}\left[(1 - 0.1) + (1 - 0.01) + \cdots\right]\]
\[= \dfrac{2}{9}\left[n - (0.1 + 0.01 + \cdots)\right]\]
Why: \(0.9 = 1 - 0.1\), \(0.99 = 1 - 0.01\), ... There are \(n\) terms, so the ones add up to \(n\).

Sum the G.P. inside
\[0.1 + 0.01 + \cdots = \dfrac{\frac{1}{10}\left(1 - \frac{1}{10^{n}}\right)}{1 - \frac{1}{10}}\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{9}\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{10^{n}}\right)\]
Why: It is a G.P. with \(a_1 = \frac{1}{10}\), \(r = \frac{1}{10}\), \(n\) terms; \(\frac{1}{10} \div \frac{9}{10} = \frac{1}{9}\).

Put it back
\[S_n = \dfrac{2}{9}\left[n - \dfrac{1}{9}\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{10^{n}}\right)\right]\]
Why: Replace the bracketed G.P. by its sum.

blocks.explanation:
The same trick as (i), for whole numbers made of one repeated digit.
Plan: take out 3, multiply and divide by 9 so the terms become \(10^{k} - 1\), then sum the G.P. of powers of 10.
steps:
Given: \(3 + 33 + 333 + \cdots\) to \(n\) terms.
To find: \(S_n\).
Method: Rewrite each term so that a G.P. appears, then use the G.P. sum.

Take out 3, multiply and divide by 9
\[S_n = 3(1 + 11 + 111 + \cdots)\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{3}(9 + 99 + 999 + \cdots)\]
Why: \(33 = 3 \times 11\), and \(9 \times 11 = 99\); also \(\frac{3}{9} = \frac{1}{3}\).

Sum the G.P. of powers of 10
\[10 + 10^{2} + \cdots + 10^{n} = \dfrac{10(10^{n} - 1)}{10 - 1}\]
\[= \dfrac{10}{9}(10^{n} - 1)\]
Why: First term 10, ratio 10, \(n\) terms. For \(r > 1\) the form \(\frac{a_1(r^{n} - 1)}{r - 1}\) keeps the signs positive (it is the same formula).

Put it back
\[S_n = \dfrac{1}{3}\left[\dfrac{10}{9}(10^{n} - 1) - n\right]\]
Why: Replace the powers of 10 by their sum.
